newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares soar 4.9 percent at close.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares soar 4.9 percent at close.

text.p: Market optimism over the possible announcement of a government package to stimulate the economy triggered heavy buying and drove share prices to close sharply higher on Monday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 35.75 points, or 4.93 percent, higher at 761.53 points.
Traders said the start of a fresh settlement period at the Delhi bourse also aided the upward trend.

"It seems that the market is depending on the government's assurance that it would announce measures for the capital markets revival, which fuelled speculative buying in blue chip stocks," said Manoj Aggarwal of brokers Choraria Investments.
Brokers said Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda might announce some steps to boost the capital markets afer a meeting with the industrialists in Bombay on Monday.
But a government spokesman in New Delhi said Deve Gowda's Bombay visit did not involve any move to revive the capital markets.
Traders said hesitation on the part of investors and local funds to sell stocks in a rising market coupled with increased speculative buy orders was stoking the price rally.
Reliance Industries was in spotlight as it jumped 12.70 rupees, or 4.9 percent, higher to 273.0 rupees.
Bourse officials freezed the upper limit on TISCO shares after the scrip surged 10 percent in a single day, after which the limit applies automatically, brokers said.
TISCO ended 18.55 rupees, or 9.83 percent, higher at 207.25.
The 100-rupee shares of ACC rose 93.0 rupees to 1,430.0.
State Bank of India rose 24.40 rupees to 295.75.
Larsen and Toubro shot up 12.20 rupees to 246.0.
